verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents draft feature revisions, review requests, required approval before publishing, commit messages, and reverting to a prior revision. Release plans and ramp schedules live in feature rules, so they are covered by this versioned revision flow. However, the evidence frames this around feature flag configuration rather than automations as a category, approval workflows sit in a higher pricing tier, and a user notes the configuration can't be kept in a code repository for config-as-code versioning and blame. Missing for 10: explicit versioning and rollback of automations themselves (ramp schedules, API- or agent-driven changes), config-as-code or Git-backed versioning, and independent hands-on corroboration of revert and review.
